Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The England players stride out to the middle. They can be seen in a huddle as the players receive some pep talk from Tom Prest. It is going to be Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Harnoor Singh who will open the innings for India. Joshua Boyden will start with the ball. Two slips in place for him. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then. 190 runs is what India have to chase. Although it is not a threatening score against this Indian batting lineup but the pressure of the final changes the dynamics. If the bowlers of England can create early pressure just like their opponents, we are in for a treat. Do join us shortly for what is going to be an enthralling chase.

James Rew is up for a chat. He says that it's a shame to miss out on a century but he is happy that his innings has given his side a chance to win the match. He adds that Sales showed good ability with the bat and that helped him play his shots as well. He mentions that they have a good bowling attack and will now look to pick up early wickets and put pressure on the opposition.

A good toss to lose for India Under-19. Indian bowlers needed a good start and boy, they got one. Ravi Kumar rattled England with two early blows. First, he got Jacob Bethell and then removed Tom Prest for a duck. After that, Raj Angad Bawa came into the attack and boy, he breathed fire. He picked four wickets and was all over the moon. He left England in the deep abyss. The bowlers just worked in tandem and never allowed the momentum to shift away. The bowlers had to work hard for the 8th wicket but after that, it was just a matter of minutes and India Under-19 got England Under-19 bowled out for 189. They will be very happy with their efforts and the pick of the lot for them was Raj Angad Bawa who becomes the first Indian to take a five-wicket haul in an ICC event final. While nothing to take away from Ravi Kumar who got 4 wickets to his name as well.

England definitely didn't hope for such a final and would have loved some more runs on the board. They had a nervy start as Jacob Bethell got out for a cheap score early on and then to add agony, their skipper - Tom Prest departed for a duck. England needed someone to do the rebuilding act and George Thomas got some runs on the board but after he got out, the English side were left dismantled. The side were struggling badly at 91/7 and needed someone to inject some momentum. It was James Rew  who got his team into the rescue act and along with Sales, they put up an much-needed partnership of 93 runs for the 8th wicket. James Rew played a sensational knock and deserved a century but had to walk back for 95. All the credit goes to him for where England finished at the end.

Utter dominance from India. The bowlers have set up the game beautifully and they will take this score happily on any given day. England would be a little disappointed but they recovered well after a horror start. It was a good pitch to bat on and opting to bat first, and have managed to put up 189 on the board thanks to James Rew who played a sensational gritty knock and was well supported by James Sales. If it hadn't been the partnership between them, England would have ended with a much lower total on the board than what they have.

OUT! TAKEN! A feather through to the keeper and Raj Angad Bawa beats Ravi Kumar to get the five-wicket haul! A wobble seam delivery, into the channel around off. The ball just straightens a bit after pitching. Joshua Boyden hangs back and has a flirt as he looks to cut. He ends up getting a faint outside edge which Dinesh Bana pouches with ease and that's his fourth catch of the innings as well. Bawa rounds up a brilliant bowling display and England have been bundled out for 189!
Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Bana b Raj Angad Bawa

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! An attempted slower one, from 'round the stumps. The ball sails over the batter's head and a wide is called.
Banged in short and angling across off. Boyden looks to have a poke at it but is well beaten.
Back of a length, around off. This is worked past point for one more.

That could have and should have been curtains on the English innings! A length ball, around off. Boyden taps it straight to point and wants to get off strike. Shaik Rasheed picks up the ball and has ample time to hit the stumps but misses. Sales wasn't even in the frame.
A length ball, angled into off. Sales opens the face off the bat and guides it through backward point for a single.
Around the top of off. Boyden keeps it out on the off side. Just the single and two wickets off it.
A yorker now, on off. Boyden manages to jam it out.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Ravi Kumar comes back into the attack and has changed the momentum of the game! Kumar comes from 'round the wicket and pushes the length ball wider of the off stump. Tom Aspinwall goes chasing after it and ends up getting a faint outside edge. Dinesh Bana makes no mistake behind the stumps and England lose their 9th. Can they reach 200 now? Also, Joshua Boyden is the last man in for England.
Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Bana b Ravi Kumar

Commentary.Commentary: Into the blockhole, on off. Tom Aspinwall jams it out.
Fuller, outside off. Sales puhses it to point for one.
Tom Aspinwall is in at number 10.

OUT! TAKEN! A much-needed breakthrough for India Under-19. Heart-breaking despair for James Rew. He deserved a century but holes out on 95. He gets a standing ovation from his teammates. He did all the repair work for his side but now has to walk back. Back of a length, on middle. James Rew gets into the positon and pulls it to deep square leg. Kaushal Tambe is stationed over there. He couldn't catch it on the first attempt. The ball pops out of his hands and failed to catch on the second attempt as well. At last, he puts in a dive and takes it one-handed. Terrific catch from Tambe. Jubilation for India but dejection for Rew and England.
Commentary.Howout: c Kaushal Tambe b Ravi Kumar

Commentary.Commentary: Huge mix-up and James Sales was a goner! On a good length, around off. Sales taps it to point and wants to retain the strike. James Rew sends him back and rightly so. Luckily for Sales, the shy at the stumps is just off target.
Fuller delivery, pushed wider and across the right-hander. Sales goes chasing after it but misses.
On a good length, angling across, outside off. James Sales looks to cut but misses.

Three dots in a row! Rajvardhan Hangargekar comes 'round the wicket now and bowls a yorker now on off. Sales pushes it back to the bowler. Rajvardhan Hangargekar does well to stop the ball on his followthrough.
Short of a length, on middle. James Sales looks to pull but gets completely beaten.
What a way to start the over! On a good length, around off, nipping away. James Sales looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Innovative now! A full toss, on middle. James Rew scoops it past the keeper to fine leg for a couple of runs.

FOUR! More runs! Floats it up, on middle. James Rew once again gets down on one knee and sweeps it really fine this time. The ball races past short fine leg and into the fence. He is playing the knock of his life here. Fantastic partnership between Rew and Sales.
FOUR! Classic! Loopy ball, outside off. James Rew gets down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg. He bags another boundary. Excellent batting from Rew.
Floats it up, on off. Driven to long off for one.

NOT OUT! Tossed up, outside off, turning away. James Sales looks to drive but misses. Dinesh Bana is lighting quick to whip the bails off. He is very confident and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replay shows that James Sales was out of the crease but did well to drag his feet back in time. Excellent work behind the stumps though.

Is that a stumping? The keeper, Dinesh Bana looks certain that he has got his man. The umpires have sent it upstairs. The replays roll in and Bana seems to be lighting quick but Sales seems to be even quicker. He just about gets the back foot inside in time. NOT OUT!
Full and on leg, pushed back to the bowler.
A tight single! Back of a length, on off. James Sales dabs it to short third man for a single. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses.
On a good length, outside off. James Sales pushes it to the off side.
On a length, on leg. James Rew pulls it to deep square leg for one.
WIDE! Short ball, on middle. James Rew sways away from the line and lets it go. Wide called for height. The partnership moves to 80 now between these two.
On the pads, clipped to mid on for a quick single.
Back of a length, outside off. James Sales cuts it past the diving point fielder for a couple of runs.
Good-length ball, outside off. Cut to point.
End of Powerplay 2! 5 fielders are allowed now outside the 30-yard circle till the end of the innings.
On off, this is pushed towards mid off.

Fullish delivery, on off. Sales drives it towards extra cover and sets off for the run in a jiffy. There is a shy at the bowler's end but it doesn't hit and it wouldn't have mattered even if there was a direct hit.
shorter in length, around off. Blocked out.
A bit width on offer. Rew strokes it off the back foot to the left of point for a quick single.
A good-length ball, around off. Rew defends it out on the off side.
Back of a length, on off. Sales pulls it towards wide mid on for a run.
A short ball, banged in around off. Sales gets on top of the bounce well and pulls it along the ground through mid-wicket for one.
WIDE! Back of a length, down the leg side. Sales shuffles across looking to pull it fine but misses. Wide called by the umpire.
Drop and run! Fullish ball, on off. Rew bunts it on the off side and sets off for a quick run.
Shorter in length, around off. James Sales hangs back and pulls it down to deep mid-wicket for another single.
Around off, this is driven on the up through the cover region for a single.
Back of a length, angling across. Rew punches it towards point off the back foot.
Around middle. Rew stays solid in defense.
What happened here? Kumar looks to bowl it from the back of the hand but ends up serving a dipping full toss, outside off. Sales looks to drive but misses due to the dip.
Back of a length, outside off. Sales taps it towards cover-point.

Leg bye! A length ball, angling down leg. Rew looks to pull but gets it off the pads and the ball goes behind square on the leg side. There is a stifled appeal from the bowler but nothing given. The batters do get a leg bye.
A touch fuller, on off. Rew gets right behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Over middle, Sales with a short-arm jab towards deep mid-wicket for one.
A good-length ball, angled into off. James Rew plays it late and guides it down to third man for a run.
On a good length, close to off stump. Rew stays deep in his crease and neatly bunts it down towards third man for a single.
Sliding onto leg, Sales shuffles across and works it to deep square leg for one.
Back of a length, on off. Sales hops to defend.
Shouts of 'Catch' but it's well short. Short ball, on middle. Rew pulls it aerially and the ball goes on the bounce to deep mid-wicket. Single taken.
A length ball, around off and angling away. Rew hangs back looking to cut but misses.
Pitched up, on off. Rew makes a watchful block.
Length again, on off. Sales blocks it out. 8 runs came off that over.
This is angled into leg. Sales keeps it out on the leg side.
A good-length ball, around off. Rew drives it on the up through point for a run.
WIDE! Length again, sliding down leg. Rew looks to whip it off the hips but misses. A wide is called.
FOUR! Hammered away! Short again, at a comfortable height and James Rew crunches the pull shot into the mid-wicket fence.
A short ball, over middle. Sales pulls it behind square on the leg side and looks for two. He has to settle for the single though.
A length ball, on the pads. Rew works it away through square leg for a single.
Floats it up, on middle. James Rew drives it past the bowler to long off for a single.
Turning away, on off. Rew defends it out.
Full and on off, squeezed back to the bowler.
FOUR! Beautiful! Well executed! Tossed up, outside off. James Rew lofts it over extra cover for a boundary.
Quicker ball, outside off. James Rew looks to cut but misses.
A full toss, on middle. Pushed to long on for a single.
A juicy full toss, outside off. James Sales thrashes it through covers but only for a run.
On the pads, pushed to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven to sweeper cover for another single. This partnership is building along nicely for England Under-19.
Flatter ball, on middle. Rew flicks it to square leg for a single.
FOUR! Nicely done! Loopy ball, down the leg side. James Rew gets on one knee and sweeps it to fine leg for a boundary.
Shortish and on off. Blocked out by Rew.
On middle, blocked on the leg side.
Flatter ball, on off. Pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, nudged to mid-wicket.
Full and on off. Kept out.
Flighted and full on off. James Rew drives it to sweeper cover for one.
A full toss, on middle. James Sales flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Angkrish Raghuvanshi to roll his arm now.
FOUR! Rew is playing a gem of an innings here. Poor ball from Ostwal. Short and on off. James Rew pulls it easily to deep mid-wicket for a boundary. He is well set and not going to miss out on those.
Shortish and outside off. James Sales cuts it through cover-point for a run.
Full and on middle, driven straight to the cover fielder.
Floats it up, on off. Driven towards covers.
Tosses it up, on off. Sales defends it out.
Loopy ball, outside off. James Rew works it off the back foot to square leg for a single.
Vicky Ostwal (4-0-14-0) is back into the attack.
Good-length ball, outside off. James Sales has a poke at it but misses. The ball goes past the outside edge.
Back of a length, on off. Sales defends it out.
On a length, on off. James Sales blocks it out from the crease.
Back of a length, outside off. James Rew punches it to point for a single.

DRINKS! James Rew gets hit on the grill of the helmet and the square leg umpire calls for the physio to have a concussion check. The umpires also call for drinks. Well then, India certainly on top of proceedings here but James Rew has shown exceptional determination to just keep the scoreboard ticking. The Indian spinners have been tight but have managed to pick up just one wicket between them. James Sales is currently providing ample support to Rew and they will try to get England as close to 200 as they can. India will look to bundle them out for under 150.

Another short delivery, on middle. This time James Rew fails to get the contact and gets hit on the grill of the helmet. There will be a little halt in play as he will have to go through a concussion test.
FOUR! James Rew is continuing on his merry way! Wonderful shot! Short of a length, on off. James Rew pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
FOUR! Excellent shot from James Sales. A touch short, around off. Sales backs away and just guide it past point and the ball races away into the fence.
The bowler, Nishant Sindhu has some issue with his shoe and needs a replacement. The 12th man runs out with an extra pair and we are ready to continue.
A loopy delivery, around off. James Sales defends it out.
Flatter delivery, on off. Sales punches it out on the off side.
Floated, around off. This is pushed towards cover.
A gritty half-century from James Rew, well done! Around off, this is driven past mid on for a single. He will now look to get his side to a defendable total.
Tossed up, wide of off stump. Rew shuffles across and plays it towards mid on.
Banged in short, around off. Sales hops and keeps it down on the off side.
Excellent running! Around middle and leg, flicked through the mid-wicket region by Sales. They push for two and get it with ease in the end.
Hangargekar is keeping a bit short and around off. Rew plays it through the cover region for one more. He moves on to 49 now.
Back of a length again, around off. Sales taps it towards cover-point for a quick single.
Back of a length, on the body. Rew hops and works it leg side for a single.
A length ball, this is driven towards mid on for a quick single. There is a shy at the non-striker's end but it doesn't hit and also the batter had just made it in time.
Nicely tossed up, on off. Sales eases it down to long off for a single.
Shorter in length, this is punched away onto the off side.
Full and drifted into middle and leg. Sales pushes it towards mid on.
Flatter one, around off. This is worked off the back foot through the cover region for a single.
FOUR! Top shot! Tossed up, on off. James Rew gets in position quickly and slogs it in front of square on the leg side and picks up another boundary.
Fuller one, well outside off. Rew presses forward and looks to cover drive but gets beaten.
A touch short and wide. Rew strokes it off the back foot through cover-point for one.
On off. Kept out by Rew.

FOUR! Sliding down leg, James Rew goes for the reverse sweep and nails it this time. Rew gets it behind point on the off side and picks up a boundary. The 100 is up for England and now they will be looking to get to 150 to give themselves half a chance in this match.
Around off. Rew defend sit out on the off side.
Tossed up, on middle. Rew presses forward to defend.
Angled into off. Rew keeps it out.

Maiden over from Nishant Sindhu. This is drifted into leg. Sales strides out looking to defend but misses. The ball hits him on the pads and there's an appeal that is turned down. Sliding down leg probably.
On a length, around off and slower through the air. James Sales stands tall and punches it towards cover.
Looped up, on off. Sales pushes it out on the off side.
A touch slower, on off. Sales goes on the back foot to keep it out on the off side.
Angled into middle. Sales blocks it out.
Lovely bowling! Quicker, around off. The ball grips and turns sharply. Sales is comprehensively beaten.
This is worked to backward square leg off the inner half for a single.
FOUR! Nice way to get off the mark! Flighted ball, on middle, turning in. James Sales tickles it to fine leg for a boundary.
Full and on off, James Sales flicks it on the leg side.
James Sales is in at number 9.

OUT! CAUGHT! Alex Horton decides to counter attack but pays the price. Kaushal Tambe gets his name into the wickets column now. England Under-19 lose their seventh wicket. Flighted delivery, around off. Alex Horton dances down the track and looks to hoick it across the line. He tries to go over mid-wicket but couldn't so as Yash Dhull leaps and completes the catch.  Just when the partnership was clicking for England, Kaushal Tambe breaks it and India will look to finish things off quickly now.
Commentary.Howout: c Yash Dhull b Kaushal Tambe

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, Alex Horton defends it out solidly.
Short and outside off. James Rew rocks back and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Flatter ball, on middle. Horton pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and on off. Rew drives it to long off for a single.
Tosses this one up, on middle. Alex Horton looks to defend. The ball goes off the inner half to square leg for a single.
Quicker ball, on off. Horton makes room and cuts it but straight to point.
Loopy ball, on off. Horton punches it to mid off.
Flatter, outside off. James Rew drags it to long on for a single.
Floats it up, on middle. Horton goes deep and works it to mid-wicket.
Full and on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Loopy ball, on middle. Alex Horton tucks it to square leg. James Rew calls for a single but Horton says no. Rew is halfway down but gets back in time.
On off, blocked out.
FOUR! Tickles this one away! Shortish, on the pads. Alex Horton tickles it fine. The outfield is very quick and the slip fielder chases it but in vain as the ball wins the race. A boundary.
Floats it up, outside off. James Rew pushes it to backward point for a single.
Short and around off, James Rew punches it off the back foot to point for a single.
Quicker, on middle. Rew blocks it out.
Tosses it up, on off. Alex Horton presses forward to block. The ball goes off the outside edge to backward point for a run.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Alex Horton pats it back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, tucked to mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Looks like Rew has decided to attack now. He moves into 30's. Slightly short from Ostwal, on leg. James Rew pulls it to fine leg for a boundary.
Full and outside off. Alex Horton looks to drive but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket.
This is eased down to long off for a single.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Tosses it up, outside off. James Rew reverse-sweeps it to third man for a boundary.

Big appeal but turned down! Tossed up, outside off, turning away. James Rew tries to defend but misses and the ball goes past the outside edge. There is an appeal for caught behind but the umpire says no.
Loopy ball, outside off. Rew keeps it out.
Floated delivery, on leg. Rew drives it to mid on.
Kaushal Tambe is brought into the attack now.
Flatter, on middle. Rew works it off the back foot through mid-wicket for a run.
On off, Rew goes for the reverse sweep but mistimes it past the slip cordon.
A low full toss, sliding into leg. James Rew sweeps it nicely behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Shorter, on off. Rew keeps it out.
Pushed through quicker and fuller, on off. Rew pushes it back to the bowler.
A touch shorter, on off. Rew defends it out.
FOUR! Sublime cover drive from Alex Horton and some respite for England. A rare bad delivery from Bawa. Half-volley, outside off. Horton leans in and strokes it through cover for a boundary.
Similar delivery, angled into off. Horton with a lovely defensive punch towards mid off.
Length again, angled in from outside off. Horton stays solid in defense.
A short ball, down the leg side. Rew pulls it down to fine leg for a single.
Peach! A length ball, on off and angling away from the left-hander ever so slightly. James Rew looks to get behind the line of the ball to block but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Pitched up, around off. Rew defends it off the front foot.
This is bowled fuller, on off. James Rew sweeps hard and through mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter, on middle. Rew blocks it out.
On off, Rew brings out the reverse sweep but can't get it past the point fielder.
On middle and leg, Rew leans in, gets to the pitch of the ball and works it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter, on a length and around off. Rew goes on the back foot to defend it out.
Tossed up, on off. Rew presses forward to defend.
Vicky Ostwal to operate now.
End of another successful over from Bawa. Just one run and a wicket off it. Length again, sliding into the pads. Horton looks to tuck but gets a faint inside edge back onto the pads.
Length again, around off. Horton defends it out.
Around the top of off. Horton stays solid in defense.

Ooh, another snorter from Bawa! Banged in short, on off. The ball just shoots up and Alex Horton is completely taken by surprise. He gets hit on the grill of the helmet and there will be another concussion check.
Alex Horton is the new batsman in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Raj Angad Bawa gets his fourth and he is over the moon at the moment. His lines and lengths have been right on the money today. This is another delivery that is delivered on a good length and bowled into that channel around off. Rehan Ahmed prods for ward and has a nibble at it. In the end, Ahmed manages to push at it and gets a thick outside edge which goes straight into the palms of Kaushal Tambe at first slip. England in a downward slump here.
Commentary.Howout: c Kaushal Tambe b Raj Angad Bawa

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up, around leg. Rew picks it up and flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
On the hips, Rehan Ahmed tickles it down to fine leg. He calls for the second run and gets it easily.
On a good length, on middle. James Rew tucks it to mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, Rehan Ahmed guides it to sweeper cover for a single.
On a length, on off. Rehan Ahmed defends it out.
FOUR! Nicely played! A welcome boundary for England. Width offered, outside off. Rehan Ahmed steers it past backward point and finds the fence.
Full and swinging away, outside off. Rehan Ahmed drives it to mid off.
Bangs a short ball, on middle. James Rew tries to pull but makes no connection on that one.

DRINKS! Rehan Ahmed gets hit flush on the helmet and the umpire calls for a mandatory concussion check. Drinks are on the field as well while Ahmed gets necessary checks done. It has been India all the way so far in the first 15 or so overs. The pacers have been at the top of their game and Kumar along with Bawa have picked up 5 wickets in between them. Apart from George Thomas, no other English batter played positively and since his departure, it's been difficult for them to get runs. James Rew though has been in the middle for quite some time now and all English hopes lie on his shoulders at the moment.

Short ball, on middle. Rehan Ahmed looks to pull but gets a top edge onto the helmet and then the ball drops in front of the backward point fielder. The batters run for a single. But there will be a mandatory concussion check.
Terrific bowling! On a good length, outside off, nipping in. Rehan Ahmed prods and looks to defend but misses. The ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Length ball, outside off. Rehan Ahmed prods and drives it but finds the point fielder.
On middle, Rehan Ahmed flicks it to deep square leg for a couple of runs. 50 up for England Under-19!
No hat-trick for Raj Angad Bawa! On a length, on middle. James Rew pokes it towards covers for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Touch fuller, outside off. Rehan Ahmed lets it sail through.
Pitched up, on off. Ahmed blocks it out.
Back of a length, on middle. Rew works it off the back foot towards mid-wicket for a single.

Huge appeal but not given! A touch fuller, into that channel around off. James Rew is brought forward and as he looks to cover drive, the ball zips past the outside edge. Th Indians are interested but the replay shows there's no bat involved.
Length again, around off. Rew pushes it out on the off side.
A length ball, outside off. Rew leaves it alone.
Rehan Ahmed comes in to bat with England in all sorts of trouble.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! England Under-19 are five down now. 'Raj Angad Bawa,' remember the name! He is the one to look out for in the future. Two wickets in two balls. This is sensational from the youngster. Everything is falling apart for England now. Raj Angad Bawa bangs it into the deck, around off and it's an absolute snorter. George Bell gets himself into an awkward position and tries to fend it away. He only manages to get some glove on it and the ball carries through to the keeper, Dinesh Bana who makes no mistake. Also, Bawa will be on a hat-trick when he comes on to bowl his next over.
Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Bana b Raj Angad Bawa

Commentary.Commentary: George Bell is in at number 6.

OUT! TAKEN! Raj Angad Bawa was probing with his line and lengths and bags his second wicket now. Indian pacers are spitting fire. This is a good pitch to bat on. As Samuel Badree mentioned - A batting paradise but the wickets keep tumbling for England. Another one bites the dust for them and it is William Luxton this time. Back of a length, outside off. William Luxton throws his hands at it. The ball goes off the outside edge and Dinesh Bana moves to his right and pouches it with both hands.
Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Bana b Raj Angad Bawa

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, outside off. James Rew dabs it to third man for a single.
Good-length ball, outside off, nipping away. James Rew looks to punch it to the off side but gets beaten on the outside edge. This is nice bowling from Raj Angad Bawa.
On a length, on off. William Luxton stays back and punches it through point for one.
Length ball, on leg. James Rew tucks it to square leg for a single.
Another good over for India! Just 2 runs from it. Loopy ball, on off. William Luxton presses forward and blocks it towards covers.
Full and on off, William Luxton keeps it out.
Tossed up, on off, turning away. William Luxton watchfully blocks it out.
Full and outside off, James Rew reaches out for it and sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy ball, outside off. James Rew presses forward and nudges it on the leg side.
Flighted ball, on the pads. William Luxton clips it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short this time, around middle. James Rew rocks back and gets on top of the bounce to pull it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Back of a length, around middle. Rew hops and defends it back onto the deck.
On a good length, around off. Luxton backs away and guides it down to third man for one more.
A length ball, angled across off. Rew opens the face of the bat and steers it down to third man for a single.
Uppish but safe! Back of a length, outside off. Luxton looks to cut but gets taken aback by the extra bounce. He manages to get it behind point and gets off the mark with a single.
William Luxton comes in with the English top-three back in the hut.

OUT! TAKEN! Dot balls create pressure and Bawa gets his man in the end! George Thomas was looking so good but sadly, has to depart. Raj Angad Bawa gets his first wicket. Length ball, outside off. George Thomas looks to swipe across the line. He loses his shape and the ball goes off the top edge and lobs towards extra cover. Yash Dhull takes the simplest of catches there and the Indian camp is pumped up. England Under-19 in trouble now.
Commentary.Howout: c Yash Dhull b Raj Angad Bawa

Commentary.Commentary: End of Powerplay 1! 4 fielders will be now allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
A bit dragged down, around off. Rew shuffles across and works it leg side. Just one run off the over and England are 37/2 at the end of the first Powerplay.
Very full and wide, turning back in a long way. Rew makes a watchful leave.
Full, on off. Thomas hangs deep and goes for the big hoick across. He gets it off the inner half of the bat towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Drifted into middle and turning away. Thomas blocks it out.
Beaten! On off and turning away sharply. Thomas presses forward to defend but is beaten past the outside edge.
A low full toss, drifted onto the pads. Thomas misses out as he sort of half-sweeps it towards backward square leg.
Maiden! A touch fuller, on middle. James Rew pushes it back to the bowler.
Five dots in a row now in this over. Length again, around leg. Rew works it towards mid-wicket.
On a good length, around middle and leg. Rew looks to tuck it leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Fullish ball, pushed across the left-hander. Rew blocks it out.
A length ball, around middle and angling across. Rew stays solid in defense.
Pitched up, on off. Rew presses forward to defend it on the off side.
Spinning in from outside off. Rew sweeps it with the spin and towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Nicely floated, around off. Rew strides out to defend.
A mandatory concussion test as Dinesh Bana is hit on the helmet. The physio is out now and is having a look at him. Dinesh Bana seems okay and we are ready to resume.

Some big turn here early on for Nishant Sindhu. Floated up, outside off. James Rew leaves it alone but the ball flicks the pad and the ball goes on to hit the keeper on the helmet. Mandatory concussion check will be done now.
Flatter, on off and turning in sharply. Rew manages to block it out.
On a length, outside off. This one turns back in. Rew watches it all the way and defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Sindhu starts off with a gentle loosener. Juicy full toss, outside off. Rew just leans in and creams it through extra cover for a boundary.

Dropped! Oh dear, that's a huge opportunity gone down. Thomas walks down the track and Bawa just pulls back his length a bit. Thomas has a poke at it and the outside edge is found. The ball sort of floats to the right of first slip and Kaushal Tambe just hesitates a bit. In the end, he drops a dolly and the big question is, how much is that going to hurt?
Length again, outside off. There's a bit of width on offer but Thomas strokes it straight to point.
A good-length ball, over off. Thomas hangs deep and dabs it down towards cover-point.
Nicely bowled! Length again, in that channel around off. Thomas looks to have a poke at it but leaves it alone in the end.
A length ball, around middle and leg. Rew flicks it towards mid-wicket for a quick single. Good running.
A fullish delivery, around off and pushed away from the right-hander. Rew let's it through to the keeper.
Raj Angad Bawa is brought into the attack. He replaces Rajvardhan Hangargekar.
Back of a length, on off. Thomas keeps it down on the off side.
FOUR! Down the pitch goes George Thomas and that shows how confident he is at the moment. Outside off, Thomas walks down the track and slaps it through extra cover for another boundary.
On a good length, on off and angling across. Thomas hangs back and nudges it down towards backward point.
Around the top of off. Thomas presses forward and defends it towards cover.
FOUR! A touch too straight and George Thomas takes full advantage. Drifting onto the pads, Thomas flicks it past short fine leg and picks up a boundary.
WIDE! Kumar looks for the inswinger, into the batter's pads but spills it down the leg side. Wided.
A touch fuller, around off and angling across. Thomas makes a watchful leave.
Fuller in length, on off. James Rew squeezes it out to the off side. Just three runs from the over.
On a good length, outside off, shaping away. James Rew leaves it untouched.
In the air, but safe! Short of a length, on middle. George Thomas pulls it into the vacant deep mid-wicket area for a single.
Length ball, attaccking the stumps. James Rew tucks it on the leg side for a single.
Full and outside off. George Thomas goes for the drive. The ball goes off the outside edge to backward point for a single.
Lovely bowling! Good-length ball, around off, moving in. George Thomas looks to defend but misses. The ball zips past the outside edge. End of a wicket-maiden over from Kumar.
Length ball, outside off. James Rew gets across and shoulders arms.
Back of a length, on middle and leg. James Rew flicks it but straight to square leg.
A yorker, on off. James Rew blocks it out.
James Rew walks in to bat at number 4.

OUT! CHOPPED IT ON! Ravi Kumar is breathing fire. He gets the England Under-19 skipper, Tom Prest and that too for a duck. Until now, no other English batter had got out for a duck in this tournament but now it is their skipper who goes for a duck and that too in the finals. Short of a length, on off. Tom Prest looks to pull but was a little early in his shot perhaps. The ball goes off the inside edge and ricochets back to dislodge the bails. India on top at the moment.
Touch fuller, on off. Tom Prest defends it back to the bowler.
On a good length, outside off. Tom Prest leaves it for the keeper to collect.
SIX! SMOKED! What a shot! Just tells you, the kind of form is George Thomas in! Short ball, on middle and leg. George Thomas pulls it with disdain and all the way over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
On a length, on leg. George Thomas looks to flick but misses. The ball hits his pads and goes through to the keeper.
Better from Rajvardhan Hangargekar! Length ball, outside off. George Thomas has a nibble at it but the ball goes past the outside edge.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Length ball, on the pads. George Thomas picks the length early and flicks it uppishly towards deep mid-wicket for another boundary.
FOUR! Nice shot! A half-volley, outside off, George Thomas cracks it through covers to get the first boundary of the innings.
Fuller, outside off. George Thomas drives it towards covers.
Full and angling away, outside off. Tom Prest tries to dig it out but misses.
The skipper, Tom Prest is in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! Ravi Kumar draws first blood! This is a dreamstart for India Under-19! Ravi Kumar bowls a good-length ball, on off, nipping in. Jacob Bethell tries to flick but he misses. He gets hit on the back pad and Ravi Kumar puts up an appeal. The umpire has no hesitation as he raises his dreaded finger. Jacob Bethell will have to walk back to the pavilion. England Under-19 lose an early wicket. Ravi Kumar is pumped up and lets out a roar.
Back of a length, outside off. Jacob Bethell meets it with a dead bat.
On the pads, Jacob Bethell flicks it to deep backward square leg for a brace. He gets off the mark as well.
On a length, outside off. Jacob Bethell guides it to backward point.

Ravi Kumar starts with a lovely delivery, on a length, outside off. Jacob Bethell looks to defend but the ball moves away. It goes past the outside edge and India Under-19 players are shouting. They think there was an edge on that. But the umpire says no. Replay shows that it was just the noise of bat hitting the pad. Good decision from the umpire.
Ravi Kumar to start from the opposite end.
A dot to end the over! Length ball, on off. George Thomas presses forward and defends it towards covers. Good start from Rajvardhan Hangargekar. Just 2 runs off the first over.

England Under-19 are underway now! A full toss, on off. George Thomas pushes it towards mid off. The fielder dives to his right and half-stops the ball. Definitely saved a boundary there. Two runs are taken!
On a length, outside off, nipping away. George Thomas is not interested in playing that one.
Excellent delivery! Good-length ball, in the fifth stump channel. George Thomas lets it sail through.
Good-length ball, outside off, shaping away. The ball is just inside the tramline. George Thomas watches it closely and leaves it alone.
Rajvardhan Hangargekar starts with a length ball, outside off, moving away from the batter. George Thomas goes for the booming drive but fails to connect.

Done with the pre-match formalities and we are ready to play! The Indian team is seen in a huddle and the English openers, George Thomas and Jacob Bethell stride out to the middle. Rajvardhan Hangargekar is ready to steam in with the new ball. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the final! The umpires are out in the middle followed by the two sets of players. They will now line up for their respective national anthems. It will be India's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of England.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree says that the pitch is a batting paradise. Mentions that there is no live grass and is hard as a rock. Tells that the ball will come on nicely onto the bat and the bowlers will need to find a way to pick wickets. Ends by saying that both teams have quality batting and also have depth in their lineup. Reckons that it is going to be a batting masterclass.

Yash Dhull, captain of India Under-19 says they would have wanted to bat first as well because it's a good wicket and reckons that it will stay the same throughout the course of the game. He adds that they take it match by match and are comfortable with batting first or second. Informs that they have made no changes to the side.

England Under-19 skipper, Tom Prest says that they will bat first. Mentions that the pitch looks good and they will look to put runs on the board. Tells that there is scorecard pressure as well and chasing in the finals is always hard. Adds that putting 230 against Afghanistan and then defending it gives them good confidence going into this game. Informs that they have not made any changes.

India Under-19 (Unchanged XI) - Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Harnoor Singh, Shaik Rasheed, Yash Dhull (C), Rajvardhan Hangargekar, Nishant Sindhu, Dinesh Bana (WK), Kaushal Tambe, Raj Angad Bawa, Vicky Ostwal and Ravi Kumar.
England Under-19 (Unchanged XI) - George Thomas, Jacob Bethell, Tom Prest (C), James Rew, William Luxton, George Bell, Rehan Ahmed, Alex Horton (WK), James Sales, Tom Aspinwall and Joshua Boyden.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it is won by England. They have elected to BAT first.

England have improved in white-ball cricket and that 2019 World Cup win has certainly inspired this generation of young cricketers, who themselves have made it to the Under 19 World Cup final. They won the competition way back in 1998 and this is the first time since that they've even made it to the final. They have their work cut out today though as they come up against arguably the nation which has dominated Under 19 cricket in the last decade or so. England have a few exciting talents themselves and their skipper, Tom Prest is certainly one of them. Then there's Jacob Bethell, Rehan Ahmed and Joshua Boyden who can cause a problem or two to the opposition. They will however need to be at their best as a team to take the trophy home. So, will England regain glory after 24 years? Or will India make it a record-extending 5th title? We'll find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

India have reached the finals of the Under 19 World Cup yet again, which makes it four times in a row now. To be honest, hardly anyone is surprised seeing them here and very few will be betting against them today as well. It was a stroll for them in the group stages and even in the knockouts, they have breezed past reigning champions Bangladesh and rivals Australia. The skipper, Yash Dhull and vice-captain Shaik Rasheed missed games in the group stage due to covid but they came back into the side and both led from the front in the semi-final, especially Dhull who even scored a brilliant ton in that match. India have a very well-balanced side and if they just play the way they have so far, it's going to be hard stopping them. The only downside for them is that they have lost 2 out of the last 3 finals in this competition.

Well, today is the day when 'Boys' become 'Men' and write their names in the history books of cricket. It's the 2022 Under 19 World Cup final and boy, it is a clash between two big guns. 4-time winners India take on 1998 Winners England at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua. Two sides who are unbeaten in the tournament but only one can lift the trophy. It should be an action-filled clash and on that note, a warm welcome to the live coverage.
